stories.title: The alien space of science: Coherent but cognitively unavailable directions
stories.author: martincsweiss

topComments.author: martincsweiss
topComments.text: Co-author here - first paper from my postdoc accepted to NeurIPS main conference. We built a way to sample diverse ideas in machine learning - ideas that make scientific sense, but that no existing research community is positioned to propose. In short, the way it works is like this: 1. Take 16,068 LLM papers (NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, ACL, EMNLP, 2017 to 2025) are broken into 273 "idea atoms". Every paper, and every candidate idea, becomes a set of atoms. 2. Train a Coherence Model: a 42.8M-parameter transformer trained on papers as sequences of atoms. Basically a language model whose tokens are ideas. 3. Train a Cognitive-Availability Model: a dual encoder trained on the publication histories of 39,791 researchers, which predicts where each person could plausibly go next. 4. Use those models to score sampled tuples using reciprocal rank fusion (you want ideas that go together well, but that are not cognitively available to anyone). We tested it in a bunch of ways. One interesting one was that we took all the papers at the end of 2024, then checked which high-scoring tuples showed up in 2025 papers. It worked well - one examples is an ICLR 2025 oral, goes from rank 1,489 with coherence alone to the top 25 of 1.14M samples. A funny one: if you ask Claude to come up with an ML research idea, it is often about interpretability. If you then run an autoresearch pipeline with some A100s on the idea, the result tends to be interpretability 8/10 times. Our Alien Sampling method stayed at 0 interpretability ideas even after letting claude cook on them. We also paid 50 people with graduate degrees in CS/AI to judge the research reports and found that Alien’s reports had the best average quality rank and produced 3 of the top 5 reports. Oh and then we scaled it way the hell up to a couple million papers and 10,000,000's of concept elements and generated 25,000 new research proposals that you can search over here: https://lacuna.tiptreesystems.com/explore?view=hypotheses Code (MIT): https://github.com/alejandrohdez00/alien-space-of-science

stackOverflowQuestions.title: Does is_mdm_removable=false affect the 30-day provisional release for Configurator-added iPhones?
stackOverflowQuestions.bodyExcerpt: I am implementing a custom MDM server for supervised iPhones using Apple Business Manager (ABM) and Automated Device Enrollment (ADE). The devices are added to ABM manually with Apple Configurator, rather than assigned by a participating reseller at purchase. The relevant ADE profile settings generated by the server are: { "is_supervised": true, "is_mandatory": true, "is_mdm_removable": false } The server also generates a separate configuration profile containing these settings (excerpt; UUIDs and other required metadata omitted): <key>PayloadRemovalDisallowed</key> <true/> <key>PayloadContent</key> <array> <dict> <key>PayloadType</key> <string>com.apple.applicationaccess</string> <key>allowEraseContentAndSettings</key> <false/> <key>allowUIConfigurationProfileInstallation</key> <false/> </dict> </array> In the implementation, that restrictions profile is sent using InstallProfile after TokenUpdate ; it is not embedded in the ADE enrollment profile. I am not treating an installation command being queued as proof that the restrictions are effective on a device. Observed behavior: during the initial 30-day period, the iPhone offers Leave Remote Management . Selecting it erases the device and releases it from management. I need to determine whether preventing that action from the first enrollment is something my MDM server can configure. I have read Apple's documentation on Configurator-added devices and the provisional period . SELECT csd.* FROM MyData csd INNER JOIN #AttributeIds id ON csd.DataAttributeId = id.ResidentialAttributeTypeId WHERE 1 = 1 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Data TRdate WHERE TRdate.PUid = csd.PUid AND TRdate.ValidDateTime = csd.ValidDateTime AND TRdate.AUid = csd.AUid AND TRdate.DataAttributeId = (SELECT ResidentialAttributeTypeId FROM ResidentialAttributeType WHERE ResidentialAttributeTypeName = 'TransferActivityEffectiveDate' AND ResidentialAttributeTypeTable = 'DataAttribute') AND TRdate.ValueDate BETWEEN @FromDate AND @ToDate) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Data cLand WHERE cLand.PUid = csd.PUid AND cLand.ValidDateTime = csd.ValidDateTime AND cLand.AUid = csd.AUid AND CLand.DataAttributeId = (SELECT ResidentialAttributeTypeId FROM ResidentialAttributeType WHERE ResidentialAttributeTypeName = 'LandUsePropertyTypeId' AND ResidentialAttributeTypeTable = 'DataAttribute') AND CLand.ValueInt = @LandUsePropertyTypeId) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Data cLand WHERE cLand.PUid = csd.PUid AND cLand.ValidDateTime = csd.ValidDateTime AND cLand.AUid = csd.AUid AND cLand.DataAttributeId = (SELECT ResidentialAttributeTypeId FROM ResidentialAttributeType WHERE ResidentialAttributeTypeName = 'MarketAreaTypeId' AND ResidentialAttributeTypeTable = 'DataAttribute') AND CLand.ValueInt = @MarketAreaTypeId) For an object, it saves about 350 attributes as row based in the table. Now, we need to get some object whose DateTime is in a range (EXISTS 1), and matches some attributes value (EXISTS 2 & 3). This above query works, however, since there are lots of objects and attributes, the query is slow. How can we optimize it? We have already created an index for PUid, ValidDateTime, AUid, DataAttributeId and try to get #AttributeIds table as small as possible. Anything else we can do?

infoqArticles.title: CSIRO Uses Serverless Architecture to Query 100x More Genomic Variants on AWS
infoqArticles.description: CSIRO has developed Serverless Beacon, a serverless architecture for querying genomic variants without copying VCF files into a central database. The system combines Amazon S3, Lambda, Athena and DynamoDB, using metadata indexes and HTTP byte range requests to query compressed genomic regions. Tests reported 1.52 second average latency for 10,000 base pair queries. By Leela Kumili
infoqArticles.author: Leela Kumili

infoqArticles.title: AWS Introduces Lambda Web Functions for Node.js Applications
infoqArticles.description: AWS recently introduced Lambda Web Functions, allowing developers to run Node.js web applications using frameworks such as Express and Hono directly on Lambda, with support for concurrent requests and response streaming. By Renato Losio
infoqArticles.author: Renato Losio

infoqArticles.title: Cloudflare Brings On-Demand CPU and Memory Profiling to Production Workers
infoqArticles.description: Cloudflare has introduced on-demand CPU and memory profiling for Workers and Durable Objects, allowing developers to investigate performance bottlenecks in production using interactive flamegraphs. By Craig Risi
infoqArticles.author: Craig Risi

infoqArticles.title: Article: Multi-Cloud FinOps: An Engineering Framework for Cross-Cloud Cost Optimization
infoqArticles.description: Multi-cloud flexibility comes with hidden egress costs driven by service placement and communication patterns. This article applies Backend FinOps to cross-cloud architecture, covering cost visibility through FOCUS, workload placement, synchronization models, and CI/CD-integrated cost governance. A controlled experiment shows architecture changes saved far more than rate negotiation alone. By Vive
infoqArticles.author: Vivek Arora

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Move Fast, Don’t Break Trust: Shipping Constantly with Humans and Beyond
infoqArticles.description: Suhail Patel discusses how Monzo structures its software engineering organization and technical stack to ship safely hundreds of times a day. He shares insights into opinionated microservice abstractions, tenancy-based staging, static analysis checks, continuous profiling, demonstrating how a strong internal platform enables engineers and LLMs to iterate rapidly without sacrificing reliability. By
infoqArticles.author: Suhail Patel

infoqArticles.title: Anthropic Adds Opt-In Security Scanning for Critical Open-Source Projects
infoqArticles.description: AI company Anthropic has launched OSS Scanner, a free, opt-in service to find vulnerabilities in open-source projects. Enrolled maintainers receive periodic security reports generated by the company's strongest models, including Claude Mythos. The reports are sent without human review, and project maintainers can choose to validate their findings and decide which proposed fixes to accept. By Matt
infoqArticles.author: Matt Saunders

infoqArticles.title: NgRx 22: Resource Extensions and Dynamic Deep Signals for Angular
infoqArticles.description: NgRx 22 adds experimental resource extensions that change Angular's resource behavior, so value() is retained during reloads and no longer throws on errors. It also introduces dynamic deep signals for union types, a SignalStoreFeatureType utility, and ESLint v10 support. Upgrading requires Angular 22 and TypeScript 6.0, and most breaking changes have automated migrations. By Daniel Curtis
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: Study Finds AI-generated Code Fails to Boost Productivity Due to Downstream Bottlenecks
infoqArticles.description: A recent Harvard study of 718 firms, using the Jellyfish analytics platform, finds that although AI coding assistants and agents increase code volume, this does not translate into a corresponding increase in completed work, partly because AI-generated code increases the workload in later stages of development, particularly code review. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Actors for Agents: Patterns for Production AI
infoqArticles.description: Manju Rajashekhar explains how the actor model solves the complex runtime challenges of production AI agents. By treating agents as distributed systems, he discusses state ownership, message passing, write-through state, and supervision boundaries to manage failures, continuations, and mutable execution graphs, moving agentic workflows beyond fragile demos to resilient architecture. By Manju Rajas
infoqArticles.author: Manju Rajashekhar

infoqArticles.title: Vercel Labs Open-Sources fx: A Zig Coding Agent Designed to Be Embedded
infoqArticles.description: Vercel Labs has released fx, an experimental open-source coding agent written in Zig. It runs as a CLI, a script component, or an embedded library, including a WebAssembly build. Early feedback questioned its model-agnostic claim and a name conflict with an existing tool. Vercel says the project is pre-1.0 and changing quickly. By Daniel Curtis
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: Article: AI Changes the Data Interface, Not the Query Engine
infoqArticles.description: This article presents a disaster-recovery analytics workflow in which an AI agent generates constrained SQL or Python, DuckDB computes reproducible facts from Parquet, and the agent interprets the results. It explains the determinism split, replayable analysis, and four signals for deciding when an embedded engine is sufficient or a managed lakehouse is justified. By Peihao Yuan
infoqArticles.author: Peihao Yuan

infoqArticles.title: Harbor Adds Docker Sandboxes to Run Reproducible AI Agent Evals in Isolated MicroVMs
infoqArticles.description: Docker announced that Harbor, the open-source agent evaluation framework, now works with Docker Sandboxes. This change allows each evaluation task to run in its own microVM. So, instead of sharing a container, tasks are isolated for better performance By Claudio Masolo
infoqArticles.author: Claudio Masolo

infoqArticles.title: Developer Behind the AI-Built Adobe Clones Says They Are “Not Anywhere Close to Ready
infoqArticles.description: A developer used Claude Opus 5.5 to build open-source replacements for seven Adobe applications, promoted them across Reddit with a projection of roughly 100% parity within a month, then told Hacker News the project was not anywhere close to ready. Its own roadmap puts it at 45% ready for real work and 2,300 to 4,100 agent-hours from full parity. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
infoqArticles.description: Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised, allowing attackers to forge certificates for any site. The keys were revealed due to low entropy, not through a known breach. Browsers blocked them using revocation lists, but other software had to remove the emSign ECC G3 root. Unpatched systems remain exposed to forged certificates, including client auth and mTLS.
infoqArticles.author: Chris Swan

infoqArticles.title: Netflix Bridges AWS IAM and Internal Identity with Workload Attestation
infoqArticles.description: Netflix has developed a workload attestation mechanism for Apache Spark jobs running on Amazon EMR. The design combines AWS IAM identity with signed claims from Netflix’s control plane before issuing short-lived internal X.509 certificates, allowing managed compute workloads to authenticate to internal services without directly injecting credentials. By Leela Kumili
infoqArticles.author: Leela Kumili
